findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "gtm_configure_source" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: gtm_sources_reference, gtm_show_sources, gtm_source_runs, gtm_configure_source, gtm_set_source, gtm_forget_harvested_posts, gtm_connect_linkedin, gtm_list_approvals · Private data: gtm_preview_source, gtm_update_icp, gtm_reject · Public sink: gtm_show_play, gtm_sources_reference, gtm_show_sources, gtm_configure_source, gtm_forget_harvested_posts · Destructive: gtm_show_play, gtm_sources_reference, gtm_show_sources, gtm_source_runs, gtm_configure_source, gtm_set_source, gtm_preview_source, gtm_run_source, gtm_forget_harvested_posts, gtm_connect_linkedin.

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
